name: Reverse Diagonal Spread (Short Diagonal)
summary: Buy the near-dated option and sell the longer-dated option at a different strike; a credit diagonal whose protection expires before the short leg does, leaving a naked position.

legs.dte_rule: front expiry, 14-30 DTE (this is the leg that dies first)

legs.strike_rule: Different strike, typically further OTM by delta 0.20-0.35.

max_profit: Limited; typically the credit received plus any gain on the front long if the underlying moves sharply before the front expires.
max_loss: UNDEFINED. After the front long expires the back-month short call is completely naked - theoretically unlimited loss on the call version, (strike x 100) on the put version.
breakevens: Path dependent; no useful closed form because the protective leg expires first.

greeks.delta: varies with the strike gap; usually modest
greeks.gamma: positive before front expiry, sharply negative after
greeks.vega: negative overall - short the longer-dated, higher-vega leg

when_to_use: Rarely, and never at level 3. The only coherent use case is a steeply contangoed term structure (back_IV - front_IV >= 6 vol points) combined with a near-term catalyst you want long gamma for. In practice it is dominated by a long front-month option plus a separate, properly covered short structure. Kept in the bank as a clearly-marked bad idea for most accounts.
entry_rules: REQUIRES ALPACA OPTIONS LEVEL 4 - the short leg outlives its cover, so the broker treats it as an uncovered short from the outset. The automation must REJECT this at level 3.
MARKED AS A BAD IDEA: any diagonal whose SHORT leg expires LATER than its LONG leg violates the core covering rule of this bank. Prefer a bull/bear diagonal with the long leg further out.
If ever traded: back_IV - front_IV >= 6.0 vol points and IV rank > 65.
Credit >= 25% of the short option's premium.
Size on full naked margin for the short leg.
Maximum 1 unit, and only on an underlying with no dividend inside the short's life.
management_rules: Close the entire structure before the FRONT (long) leg expires - there is no version of this trade that should survive its own hedge.
exit_rules: Close the entire structure no later than 5 trading days before the front (long) leg's expiry.
Close the short leg immediately if |delta| >= 0.80 or extrinsic <= $0.10.
Close the short call before any ex-dividend where extrinsic < dividend per share.
Buy back the short before selling the long.
At level 3: reject at entry. There is no management path.
assignment_risk: Worst-in-family alongside the reverse calendars: the short leg lives for months and its hedge expires first. Assignment on the short call delivers -100 shares with no cover once the front long is gone.
buying_power: Full naked margin on the short leg: greater of 20% of underlying value minus OTM amount or 10% of underlying value, plus premium.
liquidity_needs: OI >= 500 both expiries. Because exits are risk-forced, quote quality matters more than usual.
common_mistakes: Building it by accident - e.g. rolling a short leg past the long leg's expiry, which silently converts a covered diagonal into this structure. The automation must validate on EVERY roll that short expiry < long expiry.
family: Calendar and diagonal spreads (time spreads): same-strike calendars, different-strike diagonals, double/triple calendars, double diagonals, PMCC and its put mirror, LEAPS diagonals, calendarized straddles/butterflies, ratio time spreads, and the reverse (short) time spreads
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
